observations: Photo 0 and 1 show a large industrial machine, teal/green and off-white metal housing, with a row of multiple vertical needle-like arms at the top and a flat feed bed.

This configuration (multiple synchronized needle heads over a flat bed, side control panel with buttons, large footprint) is consistent with an industrial book/pamphlet thread-sewing (saddle-sewing) machine used in bookbinding, not a garment sewing machine.
No brand or model text is legible on the machine body in either photo; only a watermark 'OYOLAKFOM NIG LTD POSTED ON JIJI' is visible, which is a reseller watermark, not a maker's plate.
Machine appears used, with visible grime, rust spots on metal bed, and wear consistent with workshop use.
No power cable plugged in, no motor running, no stitched output or scrap shown to confirm function.
A person is visible in the background in photo 0, seemingly unrelated bystander/worker.
